manual-of-dual-plate.title: Manual Of Dual Plate
manual-of-dual-plate.rawHtml:
Manual Of Dual Plate 1. Introduction

A Dual Plate Check Valve (also called a double door or wafer check valve) is designed to prevent backflow in piping systems. It uses two spring-loaded plates that open with forward flow and close quickly to prevent reverse flow, minimizing water hammer. This manual outlines best practices for the valveâs lifecycle, including handling, installation, and maintenance.

2. Transportation & Storage

2.1 Transportation

ï· Keep the valve in its original packaging during handling and shipping.
ï· Use proper lifting techniques or equipment, especially for large-diameter valves.
ï· Protect the valve from mechanical impacts and rough handling.
ï· Avoid exposure to rain, moisture, and corrosive environments during transport

2.2 Storage

ï· Store in a clean, dry, and shaded area.
ï· Maintain ambient temperature and humidity to avoid condensation.
ï· Plug or cap valve ends to prevent ingress of debris or insects.
ï· Avoid stacking heavy items on the valve to prevent deformation

3. Installation

3.1 Pre-Installation Checklist

ï· Verify the valve is suitable for the intended service (media, pressure, temperature).
ï· Inspect the valve for shipping damage or contamination.
ï· Clean valve and pipeline interior to remove dust, scale, or foreign material

3.2 Installation Guidelines

ï· Ensure the flow arrow on the valve body matches the system flow direction.
ï· Install the valve between flanges using the appropriate gaskets.
ï· Center the valve properly to avoid interference with plate movement.
ï· Avoid over-torquing flange boltsâtighten bolts in a crisscross pattern to ensure even compression.
ï· Vertical installation is preferred with upward flow; horizontal installations should ensure that plates swing open easily

3.3 Piping Support
ï· Properly support upstream and downstream piping to reduce stress on the valve.
ï· Do not use the valve to support pipe weight

4. Operation

ï· The valve operates automatically based on flow direction and pressure.
ï· It requires no manual operation or external power.
ï· Sudden flow reversal or high-pressure differentials may cause premature wear or noise (water hammer).

5. Troubleshooting  Problem Possible Cause Recommended Action Backflow occurs Damaged spring or plates not sealing Inspect and replace faulty internal parts No flow through valve Valve installed backward Reinstall with correct orientation Noise or vibration Water hammer due to rapid closing Install dampeners or check system configuration Leakage around flanges Improper gasket seating or over/under torque Re-torque flange bolts and check gaskets Plates stuck open/closed Foreign material or corrosion inside valve body Remove valve, clean internals, inspect plates 6. Maintenance

6.1 Inspection Frequency
ï· Inspect every 6â12 months depending on application severity.
ï· In aggressive or dirty services, inspect more frequently

6.2 Routine Maintenance
ï· Remove valve from the line for thorough inspection.
ï· Check for corrosion, cracks, spring integrity, and seat wear.
ï· Clean all components using appropriate cleaning agents.
ï· Replace worn or damaged parts with OEM-approved components.

6.3 Reassembly and Testing
ï· Ensure all moving parts function freely before reassembly.
ï· Use new gaskets and apply uniform bolt torque during reinstallation.
ï· Pressure test valve to system specs before resuming operation.

7. Safety Precautions

ï· Fully depressurize and isolate the pipeline before removal or servicing.
ï· Wear personal protective equipment (PPE) appropriate for the service media.
ï· Use proper lifting tools and methods to handle heavy valves.
ï· Follow lockout-tagout (LOTO) procedures in industrial environments

8. Disposal

ï· Dispose of according to local regulations for metals and elastomers.
ï· Recycle metal components where facilities exist.
ï· Remove hazardous media residues before disposal

manual-of-non-return.title: Manual Of Non-Return
manual-of-non-return.rawHtml:
Manual Of Non-Return Valve 1. Introduction

A Non-Return Valve (NRV), also known as a check valve, allows fluid to flow in one direction only and prevents backflow. This manual provides guidance on handling, installation, operation, troubleshooting, and maintenance.

2.Transportation and Storage

2.1 Transportation
ï· Always transport NRVs in their original packaging.
ï· Avoid dropping or exposing the valve to impact.
ï· Secure during transportation to prevent movement or vibration

2.1 Transportation
ï· Always transport NRVs in their original packaging.
ï· Avoid dropping or exposing the valve to impact.
ï· Secure during transportation to prevent movement or vibration.

2.2 Storage
ï· Store in a clean, dry location away from direct sunlight.
ï· Maintain ambient temperatures between 5Â°C and 40Â°C.
ï· Ensure the valve ports are sealed to prevent dust or insects from entering.
ï· Avoid stacking heavy items on the valve.

3. Installation

3.1 Pre-Installation Checks
ï· Ensure the NRV size and pressure rating match system requirements.
ï· Inspect the valve for physical damage.
ï· Clean pipeline before installation to remove debris or foreign material.

3.2 Orientation
ï· Install the NRV in the correct direction indicated by the flow arrow on the valve body.
ï· Vertical or horizontal installation as per manufacturerâs recommendation.

3.3 Mounting
ï· Use appropriate gaskets and fasteners.
ï· Do not overtighten bolts â follow torque specifications.
ï· Support pipeline to avoid stress on the valve body.

4.Operation

1. The NRV allows fluid to flow in only one direction and prevents backflow automatically without manual intervention.

2. When upstream pressure exceeds downstream pressure, the valve opens due to the force of the fluid, allowing forward flow.

3. When downstream pressure becomes equal to or greater than upstream pressure, the valve closes immediately to block reverse flow.

4. The valve operates entirely based on pressure differential, requiring no handwheel, lever, or actuator.

5. Designed for minimal noise and vibration, the NRV ensures reliable sealing and performance across varying pressure conditions.

4. Troubleshooting Issue Possible Cause Solution Backflow occurs Valve seat worn or damaged Inspect and replace seat or complete valve No flow through valve Valve installed backward Reinstall with correct orientation Noisy operation High flow velocity or water hammer Reduce flow rate or install dampeners Leakage around valve body Improper flange installation or gasket damage Tighten bolts, replace gaskets Valve not closing completely Debris caught in valve or damaged internal parts Clean or repair internals 6. Maintenance

6.1 Routine Inspection

Application Type Recommended Inspection Frequency Low-risk, non-critical use Annually (once per year) General industrial systems Every 6 months High-pressure or critical systems (e.g., fire protection, oil & gas, chemical processing) Quarterly (every 3 months) Marine, aviation, or safety systems Monthly to Quarterly, depending on criticality HVAC or plumbing systems Annually, unless issues occur

6.2 Cleaning
ï· Remove the valve and flush with clean water.
ï· Remove debris or scale buildup inside the valve body.

6.3 Internal Part Replacement
ï· Disassemble the valve carefully.
ï· Replace worn parts (e.g., disc, seat, spring).
ï· Use OEM parts for replacement.

6.4 Reassembly and Testing
ï· Reassemble with care, aligning all parts properly.
ï· Pressure test the valve before putting it back in service.

7. Safety Precautions

ï· Depressurize and drain the system before servicing.
ï· Wear protective gear (gloves, goggles).
ï· Follow lockout-tagout procedures during maintenance.

8. Disposal

ï· Follow local environmental regulations for metal and rubber disposal.
ï· Clean before recycling or disposal.

manual-of-sluice-valve.title: Manual Of Sluice Valve
manual-of-sluice-valve.rawHtml:
Manual Of Sluice Valve 1. Transportation And Storage

1.1 Transportation

-Transport valves in the closed position to protect sealing surfaces.
- Use appropriate lifting equipment; do not lift the valve by the handwheel or stem.
- Avoid impact or dropping to prevent damage to valve components.

1.2 Storage

- Store in a clean, dry environment away from direct sunlight and corrosive chemicals.
- Cover the valve openings to prevent ingress of dust and debris.
- Periodically inspect and rotate valve stem to ensure functionality if stored longterm.

2. Installation

2.1 Pre-Installation Checks

- Verify the valve type, size, pressure rating, and material against service requirements.
- Inspect the valve for damage during transit or storage.
- Ensure piping is clean and aligned to prevent stress on valve body.

2.2 Installation Guidelines

- Install the valve in the correct flow direction as indicated by the arrow on the body.
- Ensure valves are fully closed before installation.
- Support the valve to avoid unnecessary pipe strain.
- Use appropriate gaskets and tighten bolts in a crisscross pattern evenly.
- Allow sufficient space for handwheel or actuator operation and maintenance access.

3. Troubleshooting

Issue: Valve leaking when closed

- Possible Cause: Worn or damaged seat or gate.
- Solution: Inspect sealing surfaces; repair or replace parts as needed.

Issue: Valve difficult to operate

- Possible Cause: Corrosion or debris on stem/gate.
- Solution: Clean components; lubricate stem; check for actuator faults.

Issue: Leakage at bonnet or flanges

- Possible Cause: Gasket failure or loose bolts.
- Solution: Replace gasket; tighten or replace bolt.

Issue: No flow despite valve being open

- Possible Cause: Gate jammed or disconnected stem.
- Solution: Inspect internals; check stem connection and gate movement.

4. Maintenance

4.1 Periodic Inspection

- Check valve operation regularly by fully opening and closing.
- Look for signs of leakage, corrosion, or mechanical wear.
- Inspect bolts, gaskets, and paint coating.

4.2 Routine Maintenance

Type of Inspection Recommended Frequency Visual Inspection Monthly Operational Check Quarterly (every 3 months) Full Functional Test Annually (1x per year) Lubrication/Servicing Annually Leakage Test Annually

4.3 Overhaul Procedure

- Isolate valve from system pressure before disassembly.
- Remove bonnet to access internal components.
- Inspect and replace worn parts such as gate, seat, stem, and seals.
- Reassemble using correct torque specifications and pressure test before reinstallation.

5. Safety Production

- Always isolate and depressurize pipeline before working on the valve.
- Use proper lifting techniques and PPE.
- Confirm absence of hazardous fluids before disassembly.
